scientific_hypothesis: Constraining the first two layers to remain near their iteration 18 optimal values (467.69 nm, 389.19 nm) with ±15 nm bounds will preserve the input coupling resonance condition that contributed to previous performance while allowing fine-grained optimization of the remaining 19 layers. The quadratic penalty beyond ±25 nm will dampen large-step excursions that may destabilize the cavity resonance.
expected_advantages: Reduces optimizer search space for boundary layers
May improve convergence stability compared to free optimization
known_risks: Anchoring may prevent discovery of better boundary layer configurations
Quadratic penalty may create local minima
21 layers may still be insufficient for dual-band requirement
expected_observations: best_target_score should increase as cavity thicknesses approach half-wave resonance at target wavelengths
tightest_margin should improve as mirror stack reflectivity increases in stopband regions
valid_candidates may decrease if cavity coupling causes unrealistic thickness requirements
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if tightest_margin becomes negative for five consecutive rounds, reduce cavity layer count by one pair and restart optimization
